p2pRoleOffererBody: Make a connect code and send it over, then wait for the one they send back.
p2pRoleAnswererBody: Paste in the code they sent, then send back the one it makes.
p2pRoleMeshBody: The server hands the connect codes around, so nobody has to pass them by hand. One person is picked automatically to relay the audio — a computer first, since it is plugged in and has a steadier connection.
p2pCodeSendToPeer: ① Send this to the other person
p2pCodeSendBack: ② Send this back to them
p2pPasteIncomingLabel: ① Paste the code they sent you
p2pPasteReplyLabel: ② Paste the code they sent back
p2pNoServerBody:
You and the other person trade one connect code, and the audio goes straight between the two devices.
Send the code however you like — a chat app, a text message, or just read it out.
p2pCaveats: ⚠️ One to one only, and there is no text, no images and no encryption badge here — those all need a server.
p2pCaveatNoTurn: Also, about a quarter of network setups cannot connect directly. Those need a relay server (TURN) filled in under settings.
p2pCaveatHasTurn: Also, about a quarter of network setups cannot connect directly. Those will go through the relay server you set up.
p2pCodeCopied: Connect code copied. Send it over.
p2pErrorNotLaresCode: That text isn't a Lares connect code. Worth another look.
p2pErrorVersionMismatch: Their Lares version is too far from yours. Update and try again.
p2pErrorCorrupted: The connect code is incomplete — part of it probably got lost in the copy.
p2pErrorWrongKind: Wrong one — that's an opening code. You want the answer code they sent back.
